seo.title: Dubai Property Return Simulator — Monte Carlo IRR | Pinzos
seo.description: Simulate 10,000 outcomes for a Dubai property investment. Purchase price, service charge and area rental yield are filled from real DLD and developer data; assumptions are labelled as such.

cdf.sub: Read it as: the chance the IRR lands at or below a given level. The dashed line is break-even.

hold.title: Holding period sensitivity
hold.sub: Bars are the median IRR; whiskers are P25–P75. All periods share the same draws, so the differences are the holding period itself, not sampling noise.

scatter.title: Price growth vs IRR
scatter.sub: 2,000 sampled runs. The tighter the band, the more your outcome depends on price growth rather than rent.

honesty.title: Where each number comes from
honesty.dldBody: Purchase price and unit size come from the developer's filed unit types. The service charge is a real AED-per-sqft rate — the project's own where we have it, otherwise the community rate from DLD owners-association filings — not a generic percentage. Rental yield is the area's median new lease divided by its median transaction price, from DLD records.
honesty.assumptionBody: Down payment, mortgage rate, loan term, holding period and growth volatility are inputs, not measurements. Change them and the whole distribution moves.
honesty.vacancyTitle: Vacancy: we have no data on this
honesty.vacancyBody: Ejari only records leases that were actually signed — a flat that never rents out never enters the database. The vacancy figure here is a market assumption with an assumed shape, not an observed value.
honesty.growthTitle: Price growth: our history is a boom
honesty.growthBody: Our transaction history starts in 2021, which covers the strongest run in Dubai's history. Using it as a forward prior overstates returns, and it overstates them in the direction that makes buying look good. That is why the default is a conservative 3% and the historical figure sits behind a button.
